chunks: 4 - Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the mines, what is in them? He said: 'Whatever is rikaz, khums is due in it.' And he said: 'Whatever you worked with your wealth, from what Allah extracted from it of its stones, purified, khums is due.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of khums on mines and extracted minerals in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the distinction between 'rikaz' (buried treasure) and actively mined minerals, establishing that khums is obligatory on both, though the latter requires prior investment of capital ('amal'). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that mineral wealth is a form of divine bounty subject to the same fiscal obligation as war booty, reinforcing the economic dimensions of the khums system in early Islamic society.
